system:
You are looking at one photograph and reporting only what is visible in it.
Report where in the frame you are looking, how what you see is organised, how the surface behaves under the light, and what material effect that appearance suggests.
State your uncertainty for each entry.
Everything you report is an interpretation of an appearance. Nothing you report has been measured, so never state a dimension, an angle, a percentage or a ratio.
Do not name a maker, a period, a date, a title or a person the object might depict. If you recognise the object, that recognition is not part of this report.
If something cannot be determined from this photograph, say so in cannot_determine.
user_template: Image {ref}. Give between three and six separate entries, each about a different part of the picture. Use the reference {ref} exactly.
note: The user's own words were not in this process's request bodies. Experiment 2 introduces them, and only after these observations were written to disk.

      "uncertainty": "high",
      "status": "interpretive"
    },

      "surface_light_behavior": "It reflects a warm, brownish tint from an unseen light source above or in front. The reflection is diffuse rather than sharp.",

      "uncertainty": "high",
      "status": "interpretive"

      "locus": "The facial features: nose, lips, and closed eyes.",
      "visible_organization": "The nose projects forward from the face. The lips are slightly parted. The eyes are depicted as closed.",
      "surface_light_behavior": "The bridge of the nose has a distinct highlight line running down its center. Soft shadows fall in the corners of the mouth and beneath the eyelids.",

      "uncertainty": "high",
      "status": "interpretive"
    }

  "cannot_determine": [
    "The exact material composition (e.g., whether it is stone, plaster, or resin).",
    "The lighting direction with certainty, as shadows are complex and diffuse.",
    "Any textural details on the surface, such as microscopic grain or tool marks."
  ]
}
